failures.claim: The bump scale is hard-coded as 1.12 (`--ui-hud-bump: 1.12`), but tokens.json already has `motion.bumpScale: 1.12`. The roll's 120 ms comes from `--duration-release`, the token for the button release, rather than a named roll/snap value. Take the bump scale from the token, as the plan audit asked ('built from tokens').
failures.evidence: hud.css: `.ui-hud { --ui-hud-bump: 1.12; --ui-hud-stamp: 1.18; }` and `.ui-hud-pos__n.is-roll { animation: ui-hud-roll var(--duration-release) var(--ease-snap); }`; tokens.json motion: `"bumpScale": 1.12`.

failures.claim: Two of the extra happy-dom tests pin internal class names instead of checking behaviour through a public seam. hud-entry-restart asserts `.ui-hud` and `classList.contains('is-entering')` plus MutationObserver records. touch-zones-entry-slide dispatches `animationend`, but no code listens for it. It passes only because zones are re-measured until GO, so the test describes a mechanism that doesn't exist.

structured_output.summary: This builds B09 HUD event motion. On a position change the Pos panel bumps (scale 1.12, stamp 160 ms) and its digit rolls up inside a clip-path box (snap 120 ms). On a new lap the Lap panel stamps from scale 1.18 with the 6px shadow landing to 3px. Both are cleared in sim time, 10 ticks after the event, and an `is-again` copy of the keyframes restarts a move that is still playing. The race entry starts from reset() through a single enter() function and ends at GO. The top panels slide down and the touch slots slide up, with 40 ms stagger delays from 0 to 0.32s. Everything sits inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so the press sink is kept. Touch zones are re-measured while the slots are moving. The stage and Chromium tests cover AC1–AC7, including the no-preference control the plan audit asked for, plus restart, window, direction and second-race cases. All gates are green. Screenshots at 844×390 and 1440×900 show the HUD and controls laid out correctly with no overlap, and matching the S1/S2 mockup. Small issues: the bump scale is a literal instead of the bumpScale token, two happy-dom tests check internal class names, and the change is somewhat larger than the expected file list.
